question.problem: Find the center and radius of the circle whose equation is ${x}^{2}-12x+{y}^{2}-16y-21=0.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the center and radius of the circle, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-12x+{y}^{2}-16y-21 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-12x+{y}^{2}-16y & =21 \\ ({x}^{2}-2\cdot 6x+{6}^{2})+({y}^{2}-2\cdot 8y+{8}^{2}) & =21+{6}^{2}+{8}^{2} \\ ({x}^{2}-2\cdot 6x+{6}^{2})+({y}^{2}-2\cdot 8y+{8}^{2}) & =121\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can factor the perfect squares and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-6)^{2}+(y-8)^{2} & ={11}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(6,8)$ and its radius is $11.$
